title: Top AI hardware stock picks from an elite fund manager
excerpt: Brandon Nelson of Calamos Investments says he's not among the "doomers" who see the end of the market's AI infrastructure trade.
content_html:
A top fund manager unpacks why he's sticking with AI infrastructure stocks, and flags 2 lesser-known names he's betting on

By William Edwards

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Brandon Nelson knows when to buy a stock.

The Calamos Timpani Small Cap Growth Fund Class (CTSIX), which he's managed since 2011, is up 52% over the last 12 months, and has beaten 99% of small-cap growth funds over the last three years, according to Morningstar data.

However, perhaps even more crucial to his success, he says, is that he knows when to sell a stock.

In an interview with Business Insider last week, Nelson said that of all the stocks he's sold since inception, the median return over the following 12 months has been -12% relative to the fund's benchmark index, the Russell 2000 Growth Index.

"We strongly believe that the biggest mistake that investors make is they sell their winners too soon and they keep their losers too long," Nelson said, adding: "We try to do the opposite."

Given that Nelson's recent outperformance has been due in large part to companies tied to the AI buildout; given all the concerns lately around their relying on hyperscaler capex; and given Nelson's knack for getting out of sinking ship, he was the perfect person to ask the question on many investors minds right now: Is it time to dump AI infrastructure names?

The trade has been red-hot for most of this year, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) up 72%. But since June 22, it's down 16%, thanks to fears that hyperscalers could start to pull back on spending as investors grow impatient to see a tangible return on all of the capex. One of the biggest questions in markets right now is whether the latest volatility is the beginning of a larger sell-off in chip makers, memory firms, and other AI hardware names.

To Nelson, the answer is no. He still sees upside for the trade, and said that the companies he's invested in haven't yet shown signs of an earnings slowdown.

When he invests in a company, he looks for growing firms that can manage investors' expectations, setting them up to consistently beat earnings. When that happens, investors grow increasingly willing to pay a higher valuation premium on the stock, he said, which leads to price upside through multiple expansion.

Then comes the skill of knowing when to sell. For Nelson, this comes down to watching for "fatigue" in the company's fundamental momentum.

Are earnings not beating expectations as strongly as they once were? Are profit margins shrinking? Then it's time to get out.

For now, at least, Nelson hasn't seen such fatigue in the AI capex beneficiaries he invests in.

"We've seen the price momentum pull back, and there's a lot of doomers out there that think that's the beginning of the end," he said. "I'm not sure I'm there yet."

He added: "The fundamental momentum of most of those AI infrastructure names is still very strong."

2 AI infrastructure stocks to watch

Nelson shared two AI infrastructure names he continues to bet on.

This first is Sterling Infrastructure (STRL), which prepares areas for data center buildouts.

"Someone's got to clear the trees and make everything flat and build roads around what's going to end up being a data center," he said. "These guys are the biggest company in the US that does this. The next biggest competitor is about one-fifth the size of Sterling."

A little over half of the company's revenues come from data center clients now, Nelson said, and it should get a boost from an increase in semiconductor and pharmaceutical manufacturing buildouts in the years ahead.

The stock is up 186% in 12 months. It's the third-largest holding in CTSIX at a 3.18% weight.

The second stock Nelson flagged is SiTime (SITM), a company that manufactures silicon timing semiconductor chips.

Data centers are one of its major customer bases, accounting for 31% of revenue, Nelson said. After its recent acquisition of Renesas Electronics, that exposure should rise even more, he said.

"Most electronic devices need this technology," Nelson said. "They've got fast growth, and they're really good at managing expectations, and these are huge markets."

Shares of SiTime have risen 190% in the last 12 months. It's CTSIX's fourth-largest holding, weighted at 3.09%.

sentences.en: He has also spent time studying or reporting in France, Germany, and Tunisia.He is based in New York.

一位顶级基金经理解释了他坚持投资人工智能基础设施股票的原因，并指出了他押注的 2 个鲜为人知的名字

作者：William Edwards 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

布兰登·尼尔森知道何时购买股票。

根据晨星公司的数据，他自 2011 年以来管理的 Calamos Timpani 小盘成长基金类别 (CTSIX) 在过去 12 个月内上涨了 52%，并且在过去三年中击败了 99% 的小盘成长基金。

然而，他说，也许对他的成功更重要的是他知道何时出售股票。

尼尔森上周在接受《商业内幕》采访时表示，自成立以来他出售的所有股票中，相对于该基金的基准指数罗素 2000 增长指数，未来 12 个月的平均回报率为 -12%。

尼尔森表示：“我们坚信，投资者所犯的最大错误是过早卖出盈利股，而持有亏损股太久。”他补充道：“我们试图反其道而行之。”

鉴于 Nelson 最近的优异表现在很大程度上要归功于与人工智能建设相关的公司；考虑到最近对其依赖超大规模资本支出的所有担忧；考虑到尼尔森摆脱沉船的技巧，他是目前许多投资者心目中提出这个问题的最佳人选：现在是时候抛弃人工智能基础设施的名字了吗？

今年大部分时间该交易一直非常火爆，iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) 上涨了 72%。 但自 6 月 22 日以来，该数字下降了 16%，原因是投资者越来越不耐烦地想看到所有资本支出的切实回报，担心超大规模企业可能会开始削减支出。 目前市场最大的问题之一是，最近的波动是否是芯片制造商、内存公司和其他人工智能硬件品牌大规模抛售的开始。

对尼尔森来说，答案是否定的。 他仍然认为该行业有上行空间，并表示他投资的公司尚未显示出盈利放缓的迹象。

当他投资一家公司时，他会寻找能够管理投资者期望的成长型公司，使它们能够持续超越盈利。 他说，当这种情况发生时，投资者越来越愿意为股票支付更高的估值溢价，从而通过倍数扩张导致价格上涨。

然后是知道何时出售的技巧。 对于尼尔森来说，这归根结底是要警惕公司基本动力的“疲劳”。

盈利是否没有像以前那样强劲地超出预期？ 利润空间正在缩小吗？ 然后是时候出去了。

至少目前，尼尔森还没有看到他投资的人工智能资本支出受益者出现如此疲倦。

“我们已经看到价格势头回落，并且有很多悲观者认为这是结束的开始，”他说。 “我还不确定我是否在那儿。”

他补充道：“大多数人工智能基础设施名称的基本势头仍然非常强劲。”

2只值得关注的人工智能基础设施股票

尼尔森分享了他继续押注的两个人工智能基础设施名称。

第一个是 Sterling 基础设施 (STRL)，它为数据中心扩建准备区域。

他说：“必须有人清除树木，平整一切，并在最终将成为数据中心的地方修建道路。” “这些人是美国最大的这样做的公司。 第二大竞争对手的规模约为英镑的五分之一。”

尼尔森表示，目前该公司一半以上的收入来自数据中心客户，未来几年半导体和制药制造扩建的增加应该会推动该公司的发展。

该股在 12 个月内上涨了 186%。 它是 CTSIX 的第三大持股，权重为 3.18%。

Nelson 标记的第二只股票是 SiTime (SITM)，一家生产硅计时半导体芯片的公司。

Nelson 表示，数据中心是其主要客户群之一，占收入的 31%。 他表示，在最近收购瑞萨电子之后，这种风险敞口应该会进一步上升。

“大多数电子设备都需要这项技术，”尼尔森说。 “他们增长迅速，而且非常擅长管理预期，而且这些市场巨大。”

SiTime 的股价在过去 12 个月内上涨了 190%。 它是 CTSIX 的第四大持股，权重为 3.09%。
